Hi Lisa / Jordan —

Great to chat this morning. Quick follow-up summary from our discovery and a short checklist so we can recommend the right deployment surface (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Key notes from the call:
- You mentioned PHI in flows and a 99.95% availability target.
- Expected peak concurrency: ~45 concurrent requests (inference calls) during daytime business hours, spiky bursts to ~120 for short windows.
- Latency target: P95 < 250ms for short prompts, P95 < 500ms for longer multi-turn sessions.
- Concern: "noisy neighbor" behavior on shared hosts causing tail latency variability.

What we need from you to finalize recommendations and a pricing sketch:
1) Confirm whether ClearHealth requires contractual data residency (e.g., specific US region) and whether PHI must be stored in your VPC only.
2) Confirm retention/access audit expectations for token-level logs (required for SOC2 / audits).
3) Clarify expected RPS sustained vs burst (% of time). The approximate numbers above are fine — if you can confirm typical sustained RPS that helps sizing.
4) Are you open to a short POC on a Dedicated pool (reserved nodes) vs spinning up a Private VPC proof-of-concept? We can do a 2-week traffic replay to validate tail latency.

Our immediate thoughts:
- Hosted API (shared): fastest to launch; cost-efficient for low to moderate steady traffic but increases risk for tail latency from noisy neighbors. Not recommended as the primary option for PHI-sensitive workloads unless paired with strong contractual SLAs and PCI/SOC2 controls.
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools with configurable autoscale and burst policies — good middle-ground for predictable latency and lower noisy-neighbor risk.
- Private VPC / on-prem: strongest isolation and control (VPC peering or on-prem appliance). Best for strict PHI/regulatory requirements; longer lead time and higher operational overhead.

I've attached a one-pager that summarizes the options. Next steps: if you can answer the four items above by EOD Friday, Monica (cc'd) and I will prepare a capacity plan + SLA examples and a short SOW draft for a Dedicated POC.

Thanks —

Ben / Evelyn — thanks for the context. Summary notes and recommended next steps below.

Short answers to ClearHealth's questions:
- "Dedicated" at Redwood means a single-tenant node pool (software tenancy isolated to you) with pinned GPU instances for your account. It does not necessarily imply dedicated, single-tenant physical GPU hardware by default — that is an option (dedicated metal) for enterprise deals but comes with higher cost and lead time. For the noisy-neighbor profile you described (bursty spikes to 100 RPS), a Dedicated pool with pinned nodes + strict autoscale and pre-warmed burst capacity will attenuate queueing pressure and reduce tail latency significantly. If ClearHealth requires physical GPU exclusivity for compliance, we can offer Private VPC or dedicated metal (quote separately).

- Token-level redaction / audit logs: we provide configurable token redaction at ingestion and full request/response metadata logs with export to your SIEM. Retention policies can be set to 12 months; we can also support a delivery pipeline to your S3 (or an on-prem archive) for long-term retention and audit exports.

- SLA examples: for Dedicated pools we typically propose availability SLA 99.9% for the pool and latency guidance (example) P95 < 250-350ms for small prompts depending on model selection and sequence length distribution. We'll supply a written SLO template in the SOW.

Capacity estimate (initial):
- Baseline: assume 20 sustained RPS -> 3 x A100-equivalent nodes (depending on model/sequence).
- Buffer for spikes: add 2 pre-warmed nodes and autoscale headroom to handle ~120 concurrent short bursts.
- POC config suggestion: 3 pinned nodes + 2 pre-warm, 2-week traffic replay using your scrubbed dataset.
- Expected outcome: validate P95 tail behavior and token cost delta between Dedicated and Private VPC.

Attachments and links: I attached a quick capacity calculator and a short playbook we use for isolation testing. Also linking our internal playbook for noisy-neighbor testing: https://docs.redwood.com/playbooks/isolation-and-dedicated-pools

Recommended next steps:
1) Approval from ClearHealth procurement for a 2-week Dedicated POC (we'll include SOW + discount for POC).
2) Provide a sanitized replay trace (or 1 hour of representative traffic) and specify the region (us-east-1 preferred).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive between ClearHealth SecOps and our infra team (30–45m) to walk through audit/log delivery and retention options.

I'll pull together the SLO/SLA language and a quick cost delta table (Dedicated vs Private VPC vs Dedicated metal) and share by EOD Monday.

Cheers,
